analysis.title: ETD Rates Watch: Jobs Shock Ignites Aussie Rates As Fed Risk Builds
key_insights: Australia's employment report showed 43.5k jobs lost against an expected 25k gain. Part-time jobs fell 40.6k and full-time jobs fell 2.9k. The unemployment rate rose from 4.7% to 4.9%.
Australian rates rallied sharply. The IR strip rose as much as 20 in the reds and 3y futures rallied 16 ticks to a high of 95.435. 3s10s steepened 4bp to 41.
UBS moved its first RBA cut call to August 2027 from November. UBS expects a 75bp cutting cycle, with further cuts in November 2027 and February 2028.
UBS Economics expects Australian real GDP growth to slow significantly and flags deterioration in the housing market and now the labour market.
The weak jobs print makes the three dissenters against the October RBA hike look, for now, like they may have been right.
US Treasuries bounced briefly on the Australian data but the move did not hold. TY traded a seven-tick range and the front end was unmoved, with the SOFR strip down one.
SOFR option flow overnight went against the recent trend of selling upside in the front end: a buyer paid 2.75 for 15k SFRH7 95.625/95.75 call spreads.
On Wednesday 67k SFRH7 96.50 calls were sold from 3.25 down to 3. It was a close-out, with open interest falling 49.5k.

FOMC minutes published Wednesday said two policymakers thought an increase of more than 25bp could be warranted in December if incoming inflation data proved unfavourable. The minutes said market expectations for hikes were broadly consistent with the Fed's assessment of appropriate policy.
The desk links the twist in the SOFR strip to Governor Waller's comments about a 50bp hike. SFRU7/U8 flattened 4bp on Wednesday to negative 16, with most of the move before the minutes.

Markets price 18bp of Bank of England hikes for December and 37bp by February. The desk does not expect back-to-back BoE hikes but would not want to sell that tail. Lombardelli's tone may give more clarity.

Thursday's central bank speakers include Lagarde, Fed Vice Chair Jefferson, BoE Deputy Governor Lombardelli and external members Greene and Dhingra. The desk says the BoE speakers are the ones to watch.
E-mini Nasdaq futures were up almost 2% as of 0700 GMT Thursday, driven by IPO enthusiasm, while Asian markets fell. Hong Kong was down 2% and Taiwan down 4.4%. Taiwan tightened short selling curbs.
The desk doubts that investors making room for IPO stocks is the whole explanation for the equity weakness in Asia, as concerns continue to hang over equity markets.
European gas prices rose 2.15% after New York Times reports that President Trump was weighing renewed strikes on Iran, while oil was flat.
The UK Treasury opposes Alan Milburn's youth unemployment proposal, a national insurance change it called hugely expensive and untargeted.

Market pricing. The desk does not expect back-to-back BoE hikes but sees the tail as not worth selling.

Deterioration in the Australian housing and labour markets.
